title: Kai microshift runbook & todo
content:
Purpose: microshift runbook for short on-call shifts (30–90m) when I'm covering infra tasks: quick checks, capacity nudges, and brief handoffs. Keep it terse; meant to be a pocket checklist + short context for follow-up.

Morning warmup (first 10m):
- Slack: #infra-ops read pinned incidents and any @ops-alert posts.
- Grafana quick glance: cluster-overview (last 1h), gpu-pool-util, pod-preempt-rate.
- Check JIRA-9123 (gpu reclaim automation) for any blocker comments.
- Note any scheduled capacity events: Dedicated pool maintenance window at 09:15 PT (expected 20m).

Quick health checks (commands I run):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels | grep gpu  # node states and zones
- kubectl top nodes | sort -nr -k2 | head -10  # spike suspects
- curl -s "https://api.redwood.local/health/serving" | jq .latency_summary  # quick latency snapshot
- nvtop or nvidia-smi -q -d PERF  # check busy GPUs on a suspect host
- sudo tcptraceroute 10.8.2.1 443  # quick connectivity if network flakiness reported

Immediate todos (priority ordering):
1) JIRA-9381: bump gpu reclaim threshold to 70% for edge pools (why: observed frequent preempts during spike) — test on staging pool 'edge-a' by 12:00.
2) Confirm Dedicated pool autoscaler had expected cooldown after maintenance; follow up with SRE if cooldown stuck. (Open PR: infra#446)
3) Add short note to Confluence draft on how prefix caching interacts with preempt reclaim (quick diagram + one example).

Triage checklist for reported latency spikes:
- Was spike global or regional? (Grafana: compare us-west/us-east)
- Which model/route? (Console -> route breakdown by model)
- Any fallback events triggered? (trace logs: fallback_count)
- If GPU queue depth high: scale target = ceil(qDepth / 8) as temporary; notify platform team before manual scale.

Commands for quick mitigation (if GPU queue stuck):
- kubectl scale --replicas=<n> deploy/edge-worker-<zone> -n serving  # ephemeral scale up
- curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.local/evict?pool=edge-a  # internal API: drains low priority pods
- rollback to model-quant-v2 (route-level) via console if quantization artifacts suspected

Notes to self (things I tend to forget):
- When draining, always set --grace-period=60 first to avoid long-lived hung jobs.
- Tag any manual changes with "kai-microshift" in GitHub PR/ops tickets.
- For cost calc: 1 extra p4d equiv ~ $3.6/hr for dedicated pool (use quick excel template).

Follow-ups / longer work items (not for the microshift but to queue):
- Build a lightweight alert that detects sustained prefix-KV misses > 30% and fires to #platform-dev.
- Write short runbook snippet for quantized-fallback behavior (where to pin, when to fallback).
- PR to infra: add small header to pool metrics that shows reclaim_ratio over last 5m.

Handoff snippet (what to tell next person):
- State: did a maintenance window at 09:15 PT on dedicated worker nodes in us-west; autoscaler seemed to reattach but cooldown lingered ~4m.
- Outstanding: JIRA-9381 change staged on edge-a; waiting for smoke tests to complete.
- Next watch: gpu-pool-util and preempt_rate for next 30m.
- Contact: Maya Li (pager) if eviction errors start recurring.

Random debugging notes (fragments):
- Saw a pattern: spike in background compactions on host g-12 corresponds with 3% drop in availability for edge-a. Could be disk IO causing NVLink stalls? Need to correlate iostat with nvidia-smi logs.
- Quick grep: logs/serving/2025-11-05 | grep -i "kv-cache miss" | wc -l => ~420 in last 10m (oof).

Personal micro-reminders:
- Water. Coffee (black) before the 10:00 standup.
- Send short note to Maya about pacing reclaim thresholds.
- If I touch infra autoscaler, add a one-line postmortem in ticket.

Open questions:
- Should we default dedicated autoscaler cooldown to 90s instead of 300s for short-maint windows? (pros: faster recovery, cons: flip-flopping)
- Is there a cheap way to simulate prefix cache churn in staging without heavy token spend? (possible: small synthetic traffic with predictable prefixes)

End of runbook snapshot. Keep this as my pocket doc—short, action-first.

---
Revision notes: 2025-11-05: added mitigations for prefix-KV miss; noted staged PR infra#446 and updated follow-ups.
